claims.text: NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 41 (1100 PM HST, Saturday, 5 September 2026): Hurricane Lowell is a Category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale with maximum sustained winds of 125 mph (205 km/h), located about 610 miles SSW of Lihue, Hawaii, moving northwest at 5 mph with an expected turn toward the north on Sunday. 'A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...The Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals' and 'A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...Kauai County, including the islands of Kauai and Niihau.' Forecast rainfall of 4 to 8 inches for Kauai, with maximum totals exceeding 12 inches possible, brings a risk of significant flash flooding and mudslides; storm surge of 1-3 feet is expected for Kauai County, and life-threatening surf and rip current conditions are expected across many of the Hawaiian Islands during the next several days.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for LOWELL-26 (reporting window 27 August - 5 September 2026) records an overall Green alert (GDACS score 0.5, low humanitarian impact) with maximum sustained winds reaching 259 km/h (Category 5); the assessment records 'no people in Category 1 or higher' wind-exposure zones because the storm has remained offshore with no terrestrial exposure through the end of its reporting window.

NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 49 (1100 PM HST, Monday, 7 September 2026): Hurricane Lowell, now a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph, was located near 21.9N 160.8W, about 90 miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, moving north-northeast at 18 mph. A Hurricane Warning (upgraded from watch) is in effect for Kauai County, including Kauai and Niihau, and for the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument; a Tropical Storm Warning (upgraded from watch) is in effect for Oahu. The core was forecast to pass just west of Niihau and Kauai overnight into early Tuesday before turning northwest and slowing.

NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 53 (1100 PM HST, Tuesday, 8 September 2026): Tropical Storm Lowell, with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph (100 km/h) and minimum pressure of 981 mb, was located near 27.3N 161.5W, about 390 miles NNW of Lihue, Hawaii, moving north at 14 mph with a forecast turn toward the northwest then west; 'there are no coastal watches or warnings in effect,' with the system weakening and moving away from the Hawaiian Islands, though swells continue to pose hazards along exposed coasts.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Hawaiʻi
claims.text: The State of Hawaii's Joint Information Center (news release HurricaneLowell-JIC-2026-002, 8 September 2026) reports Hurricane Lowell caused widespread damage to Kauai's electrical system, leaving more than 36,000 customers -- about 90% of Kauai Island Utility Cooperative customers -- without power Tuesday morning, with downed trees, utility poles and power lines reported across the island; as of 6:30 a.m. Tuesday, about 21,000 customers on Oahu were without power (14,400 Leeward, 6,600 Windward). The Hawaii National Guard had 305 personnel positioned statewide (77 on Kauai with six High Water Vehicle Teams), and multiple Kauai highways -- including Route 560 near Hanalei and Route 50 near Hanapepe -- remained closed due to downed utility poles, trees, landslides and elevated stream levels.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Hawaiʻi
claims.text: The Office of the Governor of Hawaii announced (news release, 8 September 2026) that state and county offices, public schools, University of Hawaii campuses and Judiciary facilities on Oahu would reopen 9 September 2026 as conditions improved following Hurricane Lowell, while in Kauai County, state and county offices, Kauai Community College, and all public schools on Kauai and Niihau would remain closed through 11 September 2026 as crews restore power, remove debris and address other storm impacts.

description: Hurricane Lowell, a Central Pacific hurricane that peaked at Category 5 strength in early September 2026, passed just west of Kauai and Niihau overnight into 8 September 2026 as a Category 2 storm before weakening further and moving away from Hawaii. NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center's Advisory 53 (11 PM HST, 8 September) placed Lowell as a Tropical Storm about 390 miles NNW of Lihue with 65 mph winds and no coastal watches or warnings remaining in effect. The storm knocked out power to about 90% of Kauai Island Utility Cooperative customers (more than 36,000 households) and around 21,000 Oahu customers, downed trees and utility poles, closed multiple Kauai highways, and left Kauai County state, county and school facilities closed through 11 September while crews clear debris and restore power; Governor Josh Green has deployed 305 Hawaii National Guard personnel statewide in support of the response.

impact.summary: NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory 53 (11 PM HST, 8 September 2026) placed Lowell, now a Tropical Storm with 65 mph winds, about 390 miles NNW of Lihue and moving away from Hawaii, with no coastal watches or warnings remaining in effect. Hawaii's state government reports Hurricane Lowell caused widespread damage to Kauai's electrical system, leaving more than 36,000 customers (about 90% of Kauai Island Utility Cooperative's base) without power, plus about 21,000 outages on Oahu (14,400 Leeward, 6,600 Windward); downed trees, utility poles and power lines are reported across Kauai, several highways remain closed, and Kauai County state, county and school facilities are closed through 11 September as crews restore power and clear debris. No confirmed death or injury toll has been published by an authoritative source; some media reports cite one storm-related death on Oahu, which remains unconfirmed by an official release.

name: Hurricane Lowell, Hawaii

updates.text: Lowell passed just west of Kauai and Niihau overnight into 8 September as a Category 2 storm, weakened to a Tropical Storm and moved away from Hawaii with no warnings remaining. State officials confirmed widespread Kauai power outages (about 90% of KIUC customers) plus about 21,000 Oahu outages; Kauai County offices and schools stay closed through 11 September as recovery continues.

NHC upgraded watches to a Hurricane Warning for Kauai County and the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument and a Tropical Storm Warning for Oahu as Lowell, now Category 2 with 110 mph winds, closed to about 90 miles west of Lihue ahead of its closest approach overnight into 8 September.
